what_happened: Deliverables (2) and (3) compiled on the first probe: the carrying lemma and the seven-case PlusFormula transport are OpenReversal.lean's stab/box/untl/snce cases verbatim minus ofut/opast, and the whole Plus validity-level family (plusValidOn_rev_iff, plusValidOnFrames_reflectTime, plusValidIn_reflectTime) came through with zero diagnostics via lean_run_code.

Concurrent sibling 798 declares FormalSystem.lean, FormalSystem/README.md and README.md in its file_scope; this task must add an import line to FormalSystem.lean (and a PlusLanguage README row) to register a new PlusReversal module. Overlap is a single import line in a sorted block, so a re-read-immediately-before-edit plus hunk-scoped staging suffices; flagged so the plan sequences that edit last and never stages FormalSystem.lean wholesale.

Pre-existing RED gate found at plan time, before any edit by this task: scripts/typst-sync-check.sh --counts-only reports committed status.typ formalsystem-file-count=691 / line-count=358092 vs live 692 / 358279. HEAD is already stale (stamp-commit 65ca077fd). This task adds one .lean file, which moves both counts again; typst/generated/status.typ is in concurrent sibling 799's declared file_scope, so the plan routes regeneration through a conditional, ownership-checked step rather than assuming this task owns the file.

Two corrections to the research report carried into the plan: (1) the report's Risks section names sibling 798 as the FormalSystem.lean territory contender, but dispatch 15's territory block names task 799 (798 is already complete at cdac8ab01^); (2) the report prescribes 'bash scripts/readme-inventory.sh' for the generated inventory block, but that script is a deprecated shim -- the live command is 'bash scripts/check-module-invariants.sh --emit-inventory'. (3) The report says to add one import line to FormalSystem.lean; C33 in check-module-invariants.sh asserts that file is byte-for-byte 'lake exe mk_all --lib FormalSystem' output, so the plan pins the exact sorted insertion point and forbids a hand-shaped edit.

The research report carried four compiled lean_run_code probes covering every statement this plan commits to, including the two mechanical traps (F.rev.TaskRel is the transpose not the negation; deterministic_rev needs [F.IsRegular]). Planning needed no new proof exploration -- only siting, gate, and territory work.
